title: Answer the question they actually asked
subtitle: Why prepared candidates answer a neighbouring question, how to read what a question is marking, and how to do it inside 30 seconds.
kicker: HireVue deep dive · guide two · 2027 applications

points.head: The rehearsed answer wins the race
points.text: A question that looks familiar calls up your prepared answer before you finish reading it. In real interviews, candidates gave the story that was asked for only 23% of the time.

points.head: Read for five things
points.text: Type, skill, parts, twist, instructions. Then compose one first sentence. It is the method you already use on an unseen debate motion.

points.head: Prepare to read, not to recite
points.text: 32 real questions decoded, a two-week drill plan for unseen questions, and cards to print.

meta: Prepared 26 November 2026 · Builds on the first guide · Three new research strands and 170 cited sources · Evidence limits stated throughout
how: How to read this. Sections 2 and 3 explain the problem and test whether it is yours. Sections 4 to 8 are the method: what each question wants, how to decode it, what fits in the window, and 32 real questions worked through. Sections 9 to 11 are how to practise. Section 13 is cards to print.

Sources and brackets. Bracketed names in the text are links to the source for the sentence before them. Square brackets inside example answers, like [what you found], mark facts only you can supply. “The first guide” means Pass HireVues by answering the marking scheme.
